\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সাক্ষী} (sākkhī)}{সাক্ষী (sākkhī)}]{\bn{সাক্ষী} (sākkhī) — a witness}

\label{lesson:BN-C277-sakkhi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a human being, then the Bengali for an accident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সাক্ষী}}
\textbf{\bn{সাক্ষী}} — \emph{sākkhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আগে} \bn{পাড়ার} \bn{বুড়ো} \bn{দারোয়ান} \bn{সব} \bn{ঘটনার} \bn{সাক্ষী} \bn{থাকতেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āge pāṛār buṛo dāroyān sôb ghôṭônār sākkhī thākten.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the old days the old gatekeeper of the neighbourhood used to witness everything that happened.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সাক্ষী}} (\emph{sākkhī}) is Sanskrit \emph{sākṣin}, one who sees with his own eyes, and so a witness at law (Monier-Williams). The \bn{ক্ষ} is read \emph{kkh}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sākkhī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sākkhī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āge pāṛār buṛo dāroyān sôb ghôṭônār sākkhī thākten.} — In the old days the old gatekeeper of the neighbourhood used to witness everything that happened.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a human being, then the Bengali for an accident, then say \emph{sākkhī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সাক্ষী} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A witness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কেউ} (keu)}{কেউ (keu)}]{\bn{কেউ} (keu) — someone; anyone}

\label{lesson:BN-C277-keu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an accident, then the Bengali for a witness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কেউ}}
\textbf{\bn{কেউ}} — \emph{keu} — \textquotedblleft{}someone; anyone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দরজায়} \bn{কেউ} \bn{ছিল}, \bn{কিন্তু} \bn{আমি} \bn{তার} \bn{মুখ} \bn{দেখলাম} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dôrjāy keu chhilô, kintu āmi tār mukh dekhlām nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Someone was at the door, but I didn't see their face.
\end{quote}

With \bn{না} it means no one: \bn{কেউ} \bn{এল} \bn{না}, nobody came.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কেউ}} (\emph{keu}) comes down from Sanskrit \emph{ko 'pi}, 'someone' (CDIAL 3518, which lists Bengali \emph{keu}): \emph{kaḥ} 'who' with \emph{api} 'even', whoever it may be.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{keu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{keu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dôrjāy keu chhilô, kintu āmi tār mukh dekhlām nā.} — Someone was at the door, but I didn't see their face.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an accident, then the Bengali for a witness, then say \emph{keu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কেউ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Someone; anyone\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সবাই} (sôbāi)}{সবাই (sôbāi)}]{\bn{সবাই} (sôbāi) — everyone; everybody}

\label{lesson:BN-C277-sobai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a witness, then the Bengali for someone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সবাই}}
\textbf{\bn{সবাই}} — \emph{sôbāi} — \textquotedblleft{}everyone; everybody\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আওয়াজ} \bn{শুনে} \bn{সবাই} \bn{বাইরে} \bn{এল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āoyāj shune sôbāi bāire elô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When they heard the noise, everyone came outside.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সবাই}} (\emph{sôbāi}) is \bn{সব}, 'all' — Sanskrit \emph{sarva} (CDIAL 13276, which lists Bengali \emph{sab}) — with the emphatic ending that makes it 'every single one'. \bn{সবাই} \bn{এল}, everyone came.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôbāi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôbāi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āoyāj shune sôbāi bāire elô.} — When they heard the noise, everyone came outside.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a witness, then the Bengali for someone, then say \emph{sôbāi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সবাই} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Everyone; everybody\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভিড়} (bhiṛ)}{ভিড় (bhiṛ)}]{\bn{ভিড়} (bhiṛ) — a crowd}

\label{lesson:BN-C277-bhir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for someone, then the Bengali for everyone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভিড়}}
\textbf{\bn{ভিড়}} — \emph{bhiṛ} — \textquotedblleft{}a crowd\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দুর্ঘটনার} \bn{পরে} \bn{রাস্তায়} \bn{বড়} \bn{ভিড়} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{durghôṭônār pôre rāstāy bôṛo bhiṛ hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A big crowd gathered on the road after the accident.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভিড়}} (\emph{bhiṛ}) is filed in CDIAL 9490 under a Middle Indo-Aryan \emph{bhiṭ-}, 'meet, throng', which lists Bengali \emph{bhiṛ}, 'a crowd'. \bn{ভিড়} \bn{হওয়া}, a crowd gathers.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhiṛ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhiṛ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durghôṭônār pôre rāstāy bôṛo bhiṛ hôlô.} — A big crowd gathered on the road after the accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for someone, then the Bengali for everyone, then say \emph{bhiṛ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{হাজির} \bn{হওয়া} (hājir hôoyā)}{হাজির হওয়া (hājir hôoyā)}]{\bn{হাজির} \bn{হওয়া} (hājir hôoyā) — to turn up; to be present}

\label{lesson:BN-C277-hajir-hooya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for everyone, then the Bengali for a crowd.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{হাজির} \bn{হওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{হাজির} \bn{হওয়া}} — \emph{hājir hôoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to turn up; to be present\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পরের} \bn{দিন} \bn{সাক্ষী} \bn{থানায়} \bn{হাজির} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pôrer din sākkhī thānāy hājir hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The next day the witness turned up at the police station.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{সাক্ষী} \bn{থানায়} \bn{হাজির} \bn{হল}, \emph{sei sākkhī thānāy hājir hôlô}.

With \bn{থাকা} it means to be there: \bn{সবাই} \bn{হাজির} \bn{ছিল}, everyone was there.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{হাজির} \bn{হওয়া}} (\emph{hājir hôoyā}) puts \bn{হাজির}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{ḥāḍir}, 'present, in attendance', which reached Bengali through Persian, before \bn{হওয়া}, to become: to become present, to turn up.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hājir hôoyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hājir hôoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pôrer din sākkhī thānāy hājir hôlô.} — The next day the witness turned up at the police station.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for everyone, then the Bengali for a crowd, then say \emph{hājir hôoyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{হাজির} \bn{হওয়া} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To turn up; to be present\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
